cells.tense: You are here at the choosing, and it is coming up through what you care about.
cells.act: dream it from what you have already lived
cells.ask: Build a rough picture of a want out of what you have already done — a kept note, a page of arrows, a drawing. Let that stand as the picture.
cells.core: When you pick a direction, it runs because you want it, not because you forced it. That's the whole trick, and you have it: something you care about gets chosen, the energy shows up with it, and anyone watching sees someone moving instead of someone deciding to move. It goes wrong when you skip the feeling and steer from duty alone — then the direction holds for a while and starts to feel like something you owe. This week, sit down with a want, no deadline on deciding, and pull a rough picture of it out of what you have already done — a kept note, a page of arrows, a drawing. The picture will be small and that's fine. Notice whether the next step stays easy, or starts to feel like one more thing you owe. Both are information.
cells.sheetLine: Pick the thing you actually care about and the energy shows up.
cells.verb: keeping hold of a direction long enough for it to move you
cells.place: the moment you choose on purpose and mean it

cells.tense: You are already at the following destination before the last one has landed.
cells.act: adjust one dial a little, then stop
cells.ask: Once today, take a single dial on what you're driving — time, scope, effort — and adjust it a little. Then stop there.
cells.core: The direction is real and it runs, and it's running out past every place you meant to arrive. Each goal gets reached while you are already braced for the next, so the things you actually wanted go by without the landing, and you come to rest somewhere with no memory of getting there. It isn't a lack of will. It's will pointed farther out than the road goes. So once today, take a single dial on what you're driving — the time it takes, how much of it you do, how hard it needs to be — and adjust it a little. Not by half. A little. Then stop there, and don't readjust in the morning. One correction, held, is how forward motion stays forward instead of becoming a sprint at nothing.
cells.sheetLine: The direction is real, and it's running past every finish.

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that has already closed behind you.
cells.act: mark the end of it with a plain act
cells.ask: Do a plain act that marks something as finished — clear a desk, hand back a key, close an account, write a last line and shut the book.
cells.core: The feeling is still there and it isn't moving anything yet. You know what you want and you haven't picked a direction, so it sits there in your chest and nothing leaves your hands. Being patient with it looks like wisdom from the outside and feels like standing still from the inside. That isn't a flaw in you. It's a room with a door you already went through and haven't finished closing. Do a plain act that marks something as finished — clear a desk, hand back a key, close an account, write a last line and shut the book. Nothing dramatic, no announcement, no speech. Your hands find out what your mind already knows, and when something is finished, the direction you were missing usually shows up in the space it leaves.

cells.tense: You are already moving and your account of it is that you are waiting.
cells.act: stop holding up the false thing and watch it come down
cells.ask: Stop the upkeep on something you're propping up. Let it come down, and don't rebuild it the same day.
cells.core: There's force in you that you don't count as yours. The ones close to you name it steady, or driven, or getting on with it, and you answer that you're just seeing how things go. Or the opposite: something has stopped and you can't say when or why, and you assume it's the season. Either way the thing that would tell you different isn't a speech, it's what you're holding up. Let something you're propping up come down — stop keeping it standing, and don't rebuild it the same day. The gap will show you what you were holding and why, and it knows more about your direction than any amount of thinking about it. Momentum you don't know you have is still momentum. You can't steer it while you're naming it nothing.
cells.sheetLine: The push is yours, even when you name it waiting.

attempts.check: The kernel supports 'feeling starts movement' and 'direction picked and meant' — it does not support that the person is good at endings, creatively blocked, or that momentum is missing because of an old decision. A reader could reasonably say 'my problem isn't starting, it's that I can't stop' — which is the Too Much face, not the Balanced one; keeping the four faces distinct is what earns the reading. The asks are one small act each with no promised outcome, so they stay useful even if the read is wrong; the sentence that serves me rather than them would be any line implying they're secretly visionary or secretly stalled, so I cut both. I also added the cost of keeping the balance in only the Balanced cell, where the record allows it.
